cards.title: 45-second founder video on the landing page
cards.summary: Embedding a short founder video (around 45 seconds) is credited by the source with a 33% conversion increase on the page.
cards.use_when: Adding trust and human context to a landing page for a new brand, launch, or offer where visitors don't yet know who is behind the product.

cards.title: Video testimonials as landing page proof
cards.summary: Use embedded video testimonials on the landing page as social proof that reduces skepticism before the CTA.
cards.use_when: Placing proof elements on a landing page, product page or offer page where cold traffic needs reassurance before submitting a form or buying.

cards.title: Track product-quiz or signup completion separately from purchases
cards.summary: Measure supporting store form completions without counting them as sales.
cards.use_when: When a campaign landing page collects quiz results or email signups.

cards.title: A/B test landing page variants with PostHog traffic splitting
cards.summary: Split traffic across multiple landing page variants in PostHog and let the statistical winner emerge rather than guessing.
cards.use_when: Once a landing page is live and has enough traffic, deciding between competing headlines, layouts, offers or proof placements.

cards.title: Use heatmaps and session recordings to find friction
cards.summary: Review heatmaps and session recordings to find where visitors hesitate, drop off or fail to interact before you change the page.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a landing page, PDP, cart or checkout that underperforms and you don't yet know why.

cards.title: Measure purchases separately from landing-page signups
cards.summary: Define purchase conversion as purchasing sessions divided by eligible sessions; track form completion separately.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Judge design as binary trust, not beauty
cards.summary: Website aesthetics only need to clear a trust threshold; ugly pages still convert if the offer and proof are strong.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much budget and time to spend on visual design versus copy, proof and offer for a store or lead landing page.

cards.title: Write less: control the 10% visitors actually read
cards.summary: Cut landing page copy so the headline and a few supporting lines carry the message; hide the rest for SEO.
cards.use_when: Editing a landing page or product page whose copy feels like a wall of text and where visitors bounce before reaching the CTA.

cards.title: Sell outcomes, let buyers rationalize with features
cards.summary: Lead with emotional benefits and keep features as supporting proof that buyers use to justify the decision afterward.
cards.use_when: Writing the offer block, hero copy or ad-to-page message for a store or service landing page.

cards.title: Reduce distractions on dedicated product campaign pages
cards.summary: Prioritize one product purchase path on the campaign page.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Place CTAs throughout the page and pin one on mobile
cards.summary: Distribute CTAs so the visitor can act the moment they're ready, and use a persistent bottom bar on mobile.
cards.use_when: Laying out CTAs on a landing page you're building or reviewing, especially after checking mobile rendering.

cards.title: Use a short founder video to explain product credibility
cards.summary: Test a roughly 45-second founder introduction describing why the product exists and what the founder can substantiate.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Show examples of visually differentiated products
cards.summary: Show real examples of the relevant furniture, decor or custom product variant.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Turn FAQ into an objection-handling block
cards.summary: Use FAQs to answer whatever is actually stopping people from converting, sourced from real sales conversations.
cards.use_when: Building or rewriting the FAQ section on a landing page or PDP, or when form submissions are low despite good traffic.

cards.title: Make the phone number a click-to-call on mobile
cards.summary: A tappable phone number captures high-intent visitors who want an answer now, not a form response later.
cards.use_when: Adding contact options to a mobile landing page where some visitors are in immediate-need mode rather than research mode.

cards.title: Video testimonials: 30-second self-shot clips as primary proof
cards.summary: Ask clients to record short phone-video testimonials; the presenter credits nine of them with cutting cost per conversion from $200 to $30.
cards.use_when: Building the social proof section for a store or service page when written testimonials alone feel unconvincing.

cards.title: Present documented product-use outcomes
cards.summary: Use an authentic customer or product test with a measured before-and-after result where the category supports it.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Borrow authority with brand logos, review badges and trust stats
cards.summary: External credibility markers — logos, third-party review badges, and countable trust stats — raise trust with modest effort.
cards.use_when: Filling out the trust row of a landing page or PDP where the buyer has no prior relationship with the brand.

cards.title: Make the product offer concrete and supportable
cards.summary: Name the product, intended benefit, contents and price.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Mobile-first audit with browser device mode
cards.summary: Check every landing page at phone and tablet widths before launching, since the presenter claims most traffic is mobile.
cards.use_when: Running a pre-launch QA pass on a landing page or PDP layout.

cards.title: Fix page load speed with Lighthouse, not guesswork
cards.summary: Pull the Lighthouse report and hand it to an AI agent to fix the flagged performance issues, iterating until the score is high.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a slow landing page or PDP that may be losing conversions to load time.

cards.title: Build a reusable landing page skill to multiply pages
cards.summary: Package your page structure into a repeatable generator that produces city×service landing pages on demand.
cards.use_when: Scaling from one winning landing page to many local or service-variant pages for SEO or ads.

cards.title: Improve product landing pages through measured iteration
cards.summary: Start with a clear hypothesis about product understanding, offer or purchase friction.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Verify successful form events without treating them as orders
cards.summary: For a product quiz or email signup, record confirmed completion through a success event or confirmation page.
cards.use_when: When building or evaluating an ecommerce product campaign landing page.

cards.title: Use heatmaps and session recordings to find friction
cards.summary: Watch real visitors and see where they click to locate friction points, then fix the page based on what you observe.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a page with traffic but weak conversion, when you need qualitative clues before running new variants.

cards.title: Set Up Conversion Tracking Before Running Any Test
cards.summary: Define conversion as form submit or thank-you-page view, configure a primary metric, and whitelist domains so winners and losers are measurable.
cards.use_when: Planning a landing page or PDP A/B test and you need a reliable purchase/lead conversion metric before spending traffic on variants.

cards.title: Run a 50/50 Split Test and Iterate Losers Out
cards.summary: Split traffic evenly between control and test pages, measure conversion rate, retire losers and promote winners as the new control in a continuous loop.
cards.use_when: Deciding which of two landing page, PDP or offer variants to keep, and how to keep improving after the first test.

cards.title: Use Session Recordings and Heat Maps to Find Friction
cards.summary: Review real visitor sessions and clicking heat maps to catch unexpected behavior that structured A/B tests miss.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a landing page or PDP underperforms — e.g., visitors clicking non-clickable elements, abandoning a form, or missing the CTA.

cards.title: Deploy From Localhost to a Live URL via GitHub and Vercel
cards.summary: Two-step free deployment pipeline (local code to GitHub, GitHub to Vercel) that makes the site publicly reachable so tracking, testing and heat maps work.
cards.use_when: You have a working landing page or store page on localhost and need it live so analytics, split tests, heat maps and real traffic can run.

cards.title: Treat Landing Pages as Multi-Year Assets, Not One-Off Builds
cards.summary: The source argues a well-built landing page is an upfront investment that keeps converting for years, so optimize for durability.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in a dedicated landing page/PDP build versus a throwaway campaign page, or deciding whether to rebuild an existing page.

cards.title: Native image ads: structure and when to use them
cards.summary: How native-style image ads and advertorials break scroll patterns and lower buying defenses for cold traffic.
cards.use_when: Choosing the primary ad format for a cold-traffic acquisition campaign, or deciding whether a winning video angle should be rebuilt as a native image/advertorial.

cards.title: Establish the winning angle before building the advertorial
cards.summary: Sequence: test 5+ angles in a CBO campaign first, then build an advertorial only for the statistical winner.
cards.use_when: Planning the order of work for a new product launch, or deciding whether to spend build time on an advertorial page.

cards.title: Angle-first audience selection for competitive niches
cards.summary: In saturated categories, win by picking an underserved avatar and speaking only to them rather than competing on the category's standard pain points.
cards.use_when: Product selection or campaign planning in a crowded niche (teeth whitening, supplements, personal care, etc.) where your CPMs are high and conversion is weak.

cards.title: Advertorial page structure (top to bottom)
cards.summary: The section-by-section skeleton of a converting advertorial: urgency hook, credibility figure, pain articulation, common enemy, mechanism, proof, price anchor, offer.
cards.use_when: Writing or assembling an advertorial/pre-lander page for a cold-traffic campaign where a winning angle already exists.

cards.title: Feature-to-benefit translation with the So-That Method
cards.summary: Drill every feature and desire down through repeated 'so that' questions until you hit the emotional driver, then write from the customer's perspective.
cards.use_when: Writing product page copy, advertorial body copy, or ad hooks where the draft reads as a feature list rather than a reason to buy.

cards.title: Advertorial hook and headline patterns
cards.summary: Opening patterns that work in advertorials: urgency at the top, problem-qualifying headline, and leading with price when the angle supports it.
cards.use_when: Drafting the top 2-3 screens of an advertorial or pre-lander, or testing hook variations before scaling a page.

cards.title: Spam-testing creatives: high-volume minor variations
cards.summary: Generate many variations off a winning base asset — backgrounds, placements, text colors, image swaps — to find the best-performing version fast.
cards.use_when: You have one ad or image that works and want to squeeze more performance out of the same angle before moving on.

cards.title: CBO creative testing setup and how he ran it
cards.summary: A concrete direct-response testing setup: broad targeting, automatic placements, no caps, one CBO campaign with 5 creatives, benefit-driven headlines.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new creative test campaign for an ecommerce product on Meta and deciding what to leave on default.

cards.title: Using AI to draft the advertorial in HTML
cards.summary: Prompt structure for having Claude recreate a proven advertorial structure for your brand, outputting HTML so you can preview it as a real page.
cards.use_when: You have a validated angle and want a first full draft of the advertorial page for your own product without writing it from scratch.

cards.title: Direct response design rules for the page
cards.summary: Five non-negotiable design elements: benefit headline, relevant hero, FUD reduction under the CTA, visually distinct CTA, benefit sub-headlines.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing a pre-lander, product page, or advertorial for conversion before sending paid traffic to it.

cards.title: Handling the 'why not just buy it on Amazon' objection
cards.summary: Use scarcity, exclusivity, and differentiation copy on the page to convert the portion of buyers who don't yet trust your brand.
cards.use_when: Writing the offer/proof section of an advertorial or product page where buyers can comparison-shop the same product on marketplaces.

cards.title: Scaling an advertorial into a stacked product line
cards.summary: Once an advertorial-avatar combination works, extend the same structure to adjacent avatars and product variations rather than rebuilding from scratch.
cards.use_when: Planning the next product or offer after a first advertorial-driven offer is profitable, or extending a winning page to a new audience segment.

cards.title: Page builder workflow for advertorials
cards.summary: Practical build path: generate the structure with AI as HTML, then assemble in a page builder with a free-tier option.
cards.use_when: Setting up the technical build of an advertorial or pre-lander page for a Shopify store.

cards.title: Common enemies and the gap framework
cards.summary: Create tension by naming a shared enemy (the wrong tool or method) and widening the gap between the buyer's current state and desired outcome before presenting the product.
cards.use_when: Writing the middle act of an advertorial or long-form sales page where the product introduction currently feels abrupt.

cards.title: What to keep from a winning advertorial when adapting it to a new brand
cards.summary: Transferable elements versus brand-specific ones when reusing a proven page structure.
cards.use_when: Repurposing a proven advertorial structure for a different product or store.

cards.title: Sequence an ecommerce advertorial around the next buyer objection
cards.summary: When cold traffic needs product education before reaching the purchase page.
cards.use_when: When cold traffic needs product education before reaching the purchase page.

cards.title: Align the cold-traffic ad with the advertorial hook
cards.summary: When ad clicks do not turn into engaged product-page visitors.
cards.use_when: When ad clicks do not turn into engaged product-page visitors.

cards.title: Write a specific product-use story from customer research
cards.summary: When an advertorial describes abstract benefits instead of a recognizable buying situation.
cards.use_when: When an advertorial describes abstract benefits instead of a recognizable buying situation.

cards.title: Compare real alternatives before explaining product differentiation
cards.summary: When shoppers see the product as interchangeable with cheaper alternatives.
cards.use_when: When shoppers see the product as interchangeable with cheaper alternatives.

cards.title: Explain a supported product mechanism before the offer
cards.summary: When the buyer needs to understand why product features address their problem.
cards.use_when: When the buyer needs to understand why product features address their problem.

cards.title: Match authentic product reviews to purchase objections
cards.summary: When shoppers need proof relevant to fit, use, value or reliability.
cards.use_when: When shoppers need proof relevant to fit, use, value or reliability.

cards.title: Reveal the price against a defensible product comparison
cards.summary: When the advertorial must explain value before the purchase CTA.
cards.use_when: When the advertorial must explain value before the purchase CTA.

cards.title: Close an advertorial with useful questions and genuine proof
cards.summary: When the bottom of the page leaves shoppers unsure about ordering.
cards.use_when: When the bottom of the page leaves shoppers unsure about ordering.

cards.title: Advertorials Split Selling Pressure With the Ad
cards.summary: Use an advertorial as a second force in the funnel so the ad doesn't have to carry all the selling to purchase.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to send ad traffic to a plain product page or to an advertorial/landing page before checkout.

cards.title: Validate Four Ad-Level Variables Before Building the Advertorial
cards.summary: Confirm avatar, desire, angle and unique mechanism at the ad level before investing in an advertorial landing page.
cards.use_when: Planning a new campaign or product launch and deciding whether it's safe to build an advertorial now.

cards.title: Choose Advertorial Style by Product Type: Improvement vs Innovation
cards.summary: Match advertorial format to whether your product is a better version of a known product or a brand-new innovation.
cards.use_when: Selecting the advertorial angle and length for a product before writing any copy.

cards.title: Match Advertorial Length to How Much Selling the Ad Already Did
cards.summary: Apply the selling-pressure continuum: less selling in the ad means a longer advertorial; more selling in the ad means a shorter, more direct one.
cards.use_when: Writing an advertorial lead length and deciding how soon to reveal the product, based on the current ad creative.

cards.title: Swipe Proven Advertorial Structures From Affiliate Hubs
cards.summary: Source advertorial structures from affiliate advertorial hubs, ideally from outside your own niche, to gain a structural edge.
cards.use_when: Looking for a proven advertorial layout to model before writing your own.

cards.title: Claude Advertorial Workflow: PDFs In, HTML Out
cards.summary: Feed Claude a full-page competitor advertorial PDF, an Amazon product-page PDF, and your four validated variables to get a structured advertorial in HTML.
cards.use_when: Producing a first-draft advertorial page for a Shopify store quickly, once the four ad-level variables are validated.

cards.title: Deploy Advertorial HTML on Shopify via PageFly Custom HTML Block
cards.summary: Paste Claude-generated advertorial HTML into a blank page builder page with hidden header and footer for instant Shopify deployment.
cards.use_when: Publishing a generated advertorial to a Shopify store and needing it to render as a standalone editorial page.

cards.title: Use a Quiz Funnel as a Dual-Purpose CRO and Research Asset
cards.summary: Quiz funnels simultaneously convert paid traffic into buyers and generate first-party customer data that ads and competitor research cannot provide.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to build a quiz funnel for an ecommerce store's paid traffic, or justifying the investment when quiz completion rates look lower than a normal landing page.

cards.title: A/B Test the First Three Quiz Questions as the Hook
cards.summary: The first three quiz questions function like the hook of a video and dictate total funnel throughput, so they should be tested first.
cards.use_when: Launching or optimizing a quiz funnel and deciding which element to test first to increase completion and downstream purchases.

cards.title: Structure Quizzes to Nurture and Build Conviction Before the Offer
cards.summary: Intersperse educational screens, trajectory graphs and authority proof between data-gathering questions so users are sold before they see the final product offer.
cards.use_when: Writing or redesigning the mid-section of a quiz funnel to raise completion and conversion before the sales page.

cards.title: Choose Whether to Gate the Quiz with Email Capture
cards.summary: Email capture inside the quiz boosts retargeting but can reduce front-end conversion; the right choice depends on your funnel KPIs and business model.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to require an email address mid-quiz for an ecommerce store, especially for subscription versus one-time-purchase offers.

cards.title: Generate Reports Every ~100 Quiz Submissions
cards.summary: Analyze aggregated quiz answers in roughly 100-submission batches to extract pain points, demographics and awareness stage while they are still actionable.
cards.use_when: Setting a cadence for mining quiz funnel data for product selection, ad angles and messaging decisions.

cards.title: Turn Quiz Pain-Point Frequency into Ad Angles
cards.summary: The most frequently selected quiz pain points become the hooks for new ad creatives, replacing blind competitor copying.
cards.use_when: Planning acquisition creative for an ecommerce brand when you have quiz submission data and need new ad hooks.

cards.title: Match Marketing Frame to Quiz Psychographics
cards.summary: The 'frame' — whether you lead with doctor authority, raw social proof, or logical statements — should be selected based on the psychographic data collected in the quiz.
cards.use_when: Choosing which messaging frame to lead with in ads and landing pages after reviewing quiz respondent data.

cards.title: Build the Quiz with AI to Avoid Founder Bias
cards.summary: Generate the quiz using AI with context about your product and audience so your own internal beliefs do not skew the questions.
cards.use_when: Drafting an initial quiz funnel structure before you have submission data, especially when the founder has strong assumptions about the audience.

cards.title: Use Quiz Data to Refine Product-Market Fit
cards.summary: Brands often fail to scale because their message and offer do not match a specific avatar; quiz data lets you tweak messaging, problem and frame to raise resonance.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a scaling plateau in an ecommerce store and deciding whether the issue is the offer, the message, or the audience.

cards.title: Prioritize Customer Data Over Competitor Concept Copying
cards.summary: Stop copying competitor concepts and instead use your own customers, who hold the real answers, allocating only a minor share of effort to competitor inspiration.
cards.use_when: Planning acquisition creative budgets and deciding whether to reverse-engineer competitor ads or invest in first-party research.

cards.title: Track Awareness Stage and Demographics from Quiz Answers
cards.summary: Quiz questions about prior failed solutions reveal which funnel stages and age brackets you are attracting, tuning ad targeting and message accordingly.
cards.use_when: Interpreting quiz reports to decide whether to target top-of-funnel or mid-to-bottom-funnel customers with a given ad set or offer.

cards.title: Personalize Emails by Quiz-Selected Desire
cards.summary: Because quiz integration tags users by the specific pain point or desire they selected, you can send segmented, personalized emails impossible without a quiz.
cards.use_when: Setting up post-quiz email flows for an ecommerce store to increase relevance and repeat purchase.

cards.title: Match each campaign promise to the product landing page hero
cards.summary: Repeat the paid ad’s specific promise in the campaign page or PDP hero so shoppers immediately recognize they reached the right offer.
cards.use_when: Launching or diagnosing a paid Meta or Google campaign that sends traffic to a physical-product PDP, collection landing page, or advertorial-to-product journey.

cards.title: Build a physical-product hero around outcome, mechanism, proof, and reassurance
cards.summary: A product hero should pair a clear customer outcome with an honest explanation of how the item delivers it, a direct purchase action, relevant proof, and friction reducers.
cards.use_when: Designing the above-the-fold portion of a PDP or dedicated single-product campaign page for cold traffic.

cards.title: Remove navigation leaks from single-offer campaign pages
cards.summary: For paid traffic sent to one product or bundle offer, minimize header exits so the shopper’s next decision is to evaluate and buy that offer.
cards.use_when: Creating a dedicated paid-traffic landing page for a hero product, seasonal kit, limited collection, replenishment offer, or bundle.

cards.title: Use problem–agitate–solve to connect a product to a real shopper need
cards.summary: On cold-traffic product pages, name the shopper’s existing problem, briefly establish its consequence, and immediately show the product’s credible solution.
cards.use_when: Writing the first explanatory section below the hero of a PDP, advertorial-to-product page, or product-focused campaign landing page.

cards.title: Make product-page headings and CTA lead-ins understandable to skimmers
cards.summary: Assume many visitors scan rather than read, so each heading, image, and repeated CTA must communicate the product value without relying on dense body copy.
cards.use_when: Editing a long PDP or campaign page with vague section labels, low CTA engagement, or text-heavy feature explanations.

cards.title: Close a long product landing page with a purchase recap
cards.summary: Treat the bottom of a product campaign page as a final decision block that restates the value, offer, and purchase reassurance before the shopper leaves.
cards.use_when: Building a long-form single-product, bundle, launch, or seasonal campaign page that ends weakly after reviews, FAQs, or product education.

cards.title: Optimize the ecommerce homepage for product discovery using View Product Rate
cards.summary: Treat the homepage as a route into merchandise and monitor how effectively it moves visitors from brand context into actual product views.
cards.use_when: Auditing a store homepage when traffic is arriving but category and PDP sessions, add-to-carts, or revenue are weak.

cards.title: Put purchase-critical PDP information in a scannable first screen
cards.summary: Make the product gallery, identity, rating, options, add-to-cart path, and key reassurance easy to find before shoppers must scroll.
cards.use_when: Redesigning a PDP above the fold, especially on mobile, where shoppers struggle to understand the product or reach the add-to-cart control.
